title: Early Pay Cost on Advantage Reversals, Paystride Visa Payroll Card and the Paystride Earned Wage Access Plan
content:
On the Paystride Visa Payroll Card Advantage plan, the early pay cost a reversed lost or stolen card claim is due follows the worker's Paystride Earned Wage Access Plan ledger on the claim's report day.

A claim's report day is its notice date when Paystride ordered a replacement card for a lost or stolen card on the account that day, and the claim is the most recently registered claim of its loss first reported that day. The replacement read is the stolen-card order when both a lost-card and a stolen-card replacement were ordered that day. A day with two replacement orders of the same reason is no report day. A claim's loss is the account's unauthorized-transaction claims carrying its loss date.

Of the worker's early pay transfers booked on the Paystride Earned Wage Access Plan that day to an external debit card or to a bank account, Paystride takes the most recently requested one. When two were requested at the same moment, it takes the transfer to the external debit card.

| Report day replacement | Early pay cost |
|---|---|
| card replaced as stolen | the fee booked on that transfer, less any Access reversal of that fee |
| card replaced as lost | that fee, but no more than the next-business-day bank fee of the tier the worker's Paystride Earned Wage Access Plan holds on the day the credit is figured, as the plan record shows it |
| no report day, or no such transfer | nothing |

*Hypothetical:* a stolen-card report day with a bank transfer whose fee of 1.65 was later reversed in full on the Access ledger gives nothing. The same day with an unreversed debit card transfer fee of 2.35 gives 2.35.
